definition_en: the amount of a medicine or other substance given at one time, or the way such amounts are measured and scheduled
core_image: 一支量杯里的药液刚好装到刻度线
scene: 护士核对医嘱上的剂量，确认没有超过安全范围。The nurse checked the dosage on the order and found it within the safe range.
sceneCN: 这里 dosage 是「剂量、给药量」（第 1 个义项：一次给药的量）；句意：护士核对医嘱上的剂量，确认没有超过安全范围。

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「一剂药；一次用量」，dosage 由它加后缀构成
dose 加 -meter（测量器），义为「剂量计」，用来测量辐射或药物的累积剂量
dosimeter 的词族名词，义为「剂量测定」，指测量与计算剂量的技术与学科
over-（超过）加 dose，义为「用药过量」，指超出安全范围的剂量

senses.title: A measured amount of medicine
senses.definition: the amount of a medicine given to a patient at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次给病人使用的药量
senses.example: The label states a dosage of two tablets every eight hours.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上写明剂量为每八小时两片。
senses.why: Dose came from Greek dosis, a giving, and the suffix -age turns the given portion into a measured amount.
senses.whyCN: dose 源自希腊语 dosis（给予），后缀 -age 把「给出的一份」变成可计量的量。

senses.title: A prescribed plan of dosing
senses.definition: the amount and frequency of a medicine as set out in a prescription
senses.definitionCN: 处方中规定的用量与用药次数
senses.example: The doctor reduced the dosage after the kidney test.
senses.exampleCN: 肾功能检查之后，医生降低了给药量。
senses.why: Because -age can name a collective practice, dosage also covers the whole schedule of giving doses.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -age 也能表示一种整体的做法，dosage 便扩展到整套给药安排。

senses.title: An amount of radiation absorbed
senses.definition: the quantity of radiation that a body or material receives
senses.definitionCN: 身体或材料所接受的辐射量
senses.example: Workers wear badges that record their radiation dosage.
senses.exampleCN: 工人佩戴徽章来记录所受的辐射剂量。
senses.why: The measured-amount sense extends to any agent delivered in controlled quantities, and radiation is one of them.
senses.whyCN: 「可计量的量」这一义可以扩展到任何按受控量施加的因素，辐射就是其中之一。

senses.title: An amount used outside medicine
senses.definition: the quantity of a substance added to a process such as cleaning or treating water
senses.definitionCN: 在清洁、水处理等过程中加入某物的量
senses.example: Use half the usual dosage of detergent for a light load.
senses.exampleCN: 洗少量衣物时，用平常洗涤剂用量的一半。
senses.why: Once dosage means a regulated amount, it fits any product that is added by measure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 dosage 表示「按规定加入的量」，它便适用于任何按量添加的产品。

intro.en: Dosage is dose plus the noun suffix -age. Dose goes back through French to Late Latin dosis and Greek dosis, a giving.
intro.cn: dosage 由 dose 加名词后缀 -age 构成。dose 经法语上溯到晚拉丁语 dosis 与希腊语 dosis，本义「给予」。

items.en: Dosis means a giving or a portion given, from the verb didonai, to give.
items.cn: dosis 意为给予或给出的一份，来自动词 didonai（给）。

items.en: Late Latin dosis takes the Greek noun into medical writing as the amount of a remedy.
items.cn: 晚拉丁语 dosis 把这个希腊名词引入医学写作，指药剂的用量。

items.en: Dose reaches French as the amount of a medicine taken at one time.
items.cn: dose 进入法语，指一次服用的药量。

items.en: English borrows dose for the quantity of a medicine given at one time.
items.cn: 英语借入 dose，指一次给出的药量。

items.en: The suffix -age builds dosage, first the giving of doses and then the measured amount itself.
items.cn: 后缀 -age 构成 dosage，先指给药这件事，再指所给的量本身。

items.en: Modern usage adds radiation dosage and the dosage of household products.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了辐射剂量与日用品的用量。

note.en: Dosage belongs to the dose family, and its nearest neighbours are words for amounts and intakes.
note.cn: dosage 属于 dose 词族，最近的邻居是表示「数量、摄入量」的词。

entries.definition: a single measured portion of a medicine
an instrument that measures an absorbed dose
the act of giving doses of a medicine
a quantity of something
an amount or number of something
the amount taken into the body

normalIntro.en: Dosage is dose plus -age: the amount given, and the practice of giving it by measure.
normalIntro.cn: dosage 是 dose 加 -age：既是给出的量，也是按量给药的作法。

normal.en: Dose is the base noun; dosage is the measured amount and its schedule.
normal.cn: dose 是基础名词，dosage 是可计量的量与给药安排。

normal.en: The suffix -age, as in mileage, names a measured total.
normal.cn: 后缀 -age 如同 mileage，表示按量累计的总数。

normal.en: A dosage form is the shape a medicine takes, such as a tablet or a syrup.
normal.cn: dosage form 是药物的形态，例如片剂或糖浆。

normal.en: A dosimeter measures dose, so the two words share the dose stem.
normal.cn: dosimeter 测量剂量，两个词共享 dose 词干。

normal.en: Adjust the dosage means to change how much is given.
normal.cn: adjust the dosage 意为改变给药量。

abstract.en: Picture a measuring cup filled exactly to the marked line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个量杯正好装到刻度线。

abstract.en: Picture a chart with times and amounts written in two columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表，两列分别写着时间和用量。

abstract.en: Picture a badge darkening as it absorbs invisible rays.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章在吸收看不见的射线后颜色变深。

examples.en: The pharmacist double-checked the dosage before handing over the bottle.
examples.cn: 药剂师在递出药瓶前再次核对了剂量。

examples.en: Children need a smaller dosage than adults for this syrup.
examples.cn: 这种糖浆儿童需要的剂量比成人小。

examples.en: Her daily dosage was reduced from three tablets to two.
examples.cn: 她的每日剂量从三片减到两片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多思剂」——给多少药要多想一想；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 dosis（给予、给出的一份）→ 晚拉丁语 dosis（药量）→ 法语 dose → 英语 dose；再加名词后缀 -age，构成 dosage，核心义「按量给出的一份」。

sensesIntro.en: Dosage starts from one measured portion, widens to the whole prescribed schedule, then extends to radiation and to any product added by measure.
sensesIntro.cn: dosage 从「一次量出的一份」出发，扩展到整套给药安排，再延伸到辐射剂量与任何按量添加的用品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measuring cup filled to the marked line.
core.cn: 核心意象：量杯装到刻度线。

branches.en: A single measured portion is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一次量出的一份是日常义项。

branches.en: A prescribed plan grows out of repeated portions.
branches.cn: 给药方案由反复给出的份量长成。

branches.en: Radiation dose borrows the measured-amount image.
branches.cn: 辐射剂量借用了「可计量的量」这一意象。

branches.en: Detergent dosage applies the same image outside medicine.
branches.cn: 洗涤剂用量把同一意象用到医学之外。

branches.en: A written order joins the amount and the timetable.
branches.cn: 一纸医嘱把用量与时间表连在一起。

intro.en: Dosage is built from dose and the noun suffix -age, with doser and dosimeter in the same family.
intro.cn: dosage 由 dose 与名词后缀 -age 构成，同族还有 doser 与 dosimeter。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin dosis, from Greek dosis, a giving, supplies the base for dose and dosage.
latinIntro.cn: 晚拉丁语 dosis 来自希腊语 dosis（给予），是 dose 与 dosage 的来源。

items.meaning: a measured portion of a medicine
items.example: Dose is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: dose 是这个词族的基础名词。

items.meaning: to give a measured amount to someone
items.example: Nurses dose patients by body weight.
items.exampleCN: 护士按体重给病人用药。

items.meaning: a person or device that gives doses
items.meaningCN: 给量者；按剂量给药的人或装置
items.example: A doser delivers the syrup in fixed amounts.
items.exampleCN: doser 按固定量送出糖浆。

items.meaningCN: 表示集合或计量总数的后缀
items.example: The suffix -age forms dosage from dose.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 由 dose 构成 dosage。

items.meaning: the amount given and its schedule
items.example: Dosage names the measured amount.
items.exampleCN: dosage 指可计量的给药量。

items.example: Dosing follows a fixed timetable.
items.exampleCN: 给药按固定时间表进行。

items.example: A dosimeter records the radiation dose.
items.exampleCN: dosimeter 记录辐射剂量。

items.example: Dosimetry guides radiotherapy.
items.exampleCN: 剂量测定指导放射治疗。

items.meaning: a dose larger than is safe
items.example: An overdose can be fatal.
items.exampleCN: 用药过量可能致命。

definition_en: the act of putting blood or another fluid into the body through a vein, or the amount so given
core_image: 一袋血液经细管缓缓流进手臂静脉
scene: 手术中出现大量失血，医生决定立刻输血。During the operation the surgeon decided to give a transfusion at once.
sceneCN: 这里 transfusion 是「输血」（第 1 个义项：把血液输入病人体内）；句意：手术中出现大量失血，医生决定立刻输血。

derivatives.zh: 动词形式，trans-（越过）加 fundere（倒），义为「输血；输注」
transfusion 加 -al，义为「输血的；与输血有关的」
auto-（自身）加 transfusion，义为「自体输血」，把病人先前采集的血液回输

senses.title: Blood poured into a vein
senses.definition: the giving of blood from a donor into a patient vein
senses.definitionCN: 把供血者的血液输入病人静脉
senses.example: She needed a transfusion after losing blood in the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 她在事故中失血，需要输血。
senses.why: Latin transfundere means to pour across, so the first sense is blood poured from one body into another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 transfundere 意为「倒过去」，所以第一个义项就是把血从一具身体倒进另一具身体。

senses.title: A transfusion of one component
senses.definition: the giving of a single blood component such as plasma, platelets, or red cells
senses.definitionCN: 只输入某一种血液成分，如血浆、血小板或红细胞
senses.example: A transfusion of platelets stopped the bleeding within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 输注血小板后，出血在一小时内止住了。
senses.why: Once blood is separated into parts, each part can be poured across on its own, so the word follows the component.
senses.whyCN: 血液被分离成各种成分后，每种成分都能单独输注，于是这个词跟着成分走。

senses.title: Any fluid given by vein
senses.definition: the slow introduction of a liquid such as saline or a drug into a vein
senses.definitionCN: 把生理盐水或药物等液体缓慢输入静脉
senses.example: The nurse began a transfusion of saline before the scan.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描前护士开始给病人输生理盐水。
senses.why: The pouring image does not depend on blood, so looser use extends the word to any fluid poured into a vein.
senses.whyCN: 「倒进去」的意象并不依赖血液，较宽的用法便把此词扩到任何输入静脉的液体。

senses.title: A fresh supply of something
senses.definition: a large addition of money, ideas, or people that revives an organization
senses.definitionCN: 为机构注入大量资金、思想或人员，使其重新振作
senses.example: The grant was a transfusion of money for the closing clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款对那家快要关门的诊所来说是一笔输血式的资金。
senses.why: Because the word pictures life poured into a weak body, it easily becomes a figure for renewing anything that is failing.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词画的是把生机倒进虚弱的身体，它很容易变成让任何衰败事物重获生机的比喻。

intro.en: Transfusion comes from Latin transfusio, a pouring across, from transfundere, to pour across: trans-, across, plus fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: transfusion 来自拉丁语 transfusio（倒过去），源自动词 transfundere（倒过去）：trans-（越过）加 fundere（倒）。

items.en: Fundere means to pour, with the supine fusum supplying the stem found in transfusion.
items.cn: fundere 意为倒、倾注，其目的分词 fusum 提供 transfusion 中见到的词干。

items.en: Transfundere joins trans-, across, to fundere, so the verb means to pour from one vessel into another.
items.cn: transfundere 把 trans-（越过）与 fundere 结合，动词意为把液体从一器皿倒进另一器皿。

items.en: Transfusio names the pouring across, first of liquids and later of blood.
items.cn: transfusio 指倾倒转移，先用于液体，后来用于血液。

items.en: English adopts transfusion for the transfer of blood, after early experiments on animals.
items.cn: 在早期动物实验之后，英语用 transfusion 指血液的转移。

items.en: Transfusion becomes a measured clinical procedure with volumes, reactions, and records.
items.cn: transfusion 成为有计量、有反应记录、有档案的临床操作。

items.en: Component therapy extends transfusion to plasma, platelets, and red cells given separately.
items.cn: 成分治疗把 transfusion 扩展到分别输注的血浆、血小板与红细胞。

note.en: Transfusion shares the -fus- pouring stem with infusion and perfusion, and sits beside words for giving fluid.
note.cn: transfusion 与 infusion、perfusion 共享表示「倒」的 -fus- 词干，并与表示输入液体的词相邻。

entries.definition: to transfer blood or fluid into a vein
relating to a transfusion
the return of blood collected earlier from the same patient
entries.definitionCN: 自体输血，把先前从同一病人采集的血液回输

entries.definition: the slow giving of fluid or a drug into a vein
the forcing of a liquid into the body with a syringe
a slow flow of fluid into a vein, or the apparatus for it

normalIntro.en: Transfusion is a pouring across: trans- carries the across, and the -fus- stem carries the pour.
normalIntro.cn: transfusion 是「倒过去」：trans- 带「越过」，-fus- 词干带「倒」。

normal.en: Trans- means across, and fundere means to pour, so a transfusion pours blood across into a vein.
normal.cn: trans- 意为越过，fundere 意为倒，所以 transfusion 就是把血倒进静脉。

normal.en: Transfuse is the verb and transfusion is the noun for the same act.
normal.cn: transfuse 是动词，transfusion 是同一动作的名词。

normal.en: A transfusion reaction means the body rejects the poured blood.
normal.cn: transfusion reaction 意为身体对输入的血产生排斥反应。

normal.en: Autotransfusion returns blood that was collected earlier to the same person.
normal.cn: autotransfusion 把先前采集的血回输给同一个人。

normal.en: In writing about money, a transfusion of funds means a fresh supply that keeps a body alive.
normal.cn: 写资金时，a transfusion of funds 指让机构活下去的新鲜补给。

abstract.en: Picture a bag of blood hanging above a bed, its tube leading to an arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋血挂在床头上方，细管连到手臂。

abstract.en: Picture three small bags side by side: red cells, plasma, and platelets.
abstract.cn: 想象三个小袋并排：红细胞、血浆、血小板。

abstract.en: Picture a clear bag of saline dripping steadily into a vein.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋清亮的生理盐水一滴一滴稳稳流入静脉。

examples.en: The patient received a transfusion of two units of blood after the crash.
examples.cn: 事故之后，病人输了两单位血。

examples.en: A transfusion is ordered when the blood count falls too low.
examples.cn: 血细胞计数过低时就会安排输血。

examples.en: The hospital keeps a transfusion record for every unit given.
examples.cn: 医院为每一单位输入的血液保留输血记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「传思扶」——把血传过去、扶住病人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（越过、穿过）加 fundere（倒、倾注）→ transfundere（倒过去、转移）→ transfusio（倾倒、转移）→ 法语 transfusion → 英语 transfusion，核心义「把液体从一处倒进另一处」。

sensesIntro.en: Transfusion begins with blood poured across into a vein, narrows into single components, loosens into any fluid given by vein, and finally becomes a figure for a fresh supply.
sensesIntro.cn: transfusion 从「把血倒进静脉」开始，收窄为单一成分输注，放宽为任何静脉输入的液体，最后成为「注入新鲜力量」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag of blood flowing through a tube into an arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一袋血经细管流入手臂。

branches.en: Whole blood poured across is the original sense.
branches.cn: 整血倒过去是最初的义项。

branches.en: Single components refine the same pouring act.
branches.cn: 单一成分是同一「倒」的动作的细分。

branches.en: Any fluid in a vein keeps only the pouring image.
branches.cn: 任何液体入静脉只保留了「倒」的意象。

branches.en: A grant poured into a weak body is the figurative branch.
branches.cn: 把拨款倒进虚弱机构，是比喻分支。

branches.en: Blood and saline travel by the same tube and the same verb.
branches.cn: 血液与盐水走同一根管子，也用同一个动词。

intro.en: Transfusion is trans- plus the -fus- stem of fundere, with transfuse and transfusional built on the same base.
intro.cn: transfusion 由 trans- 加 fundere 的 -fus- 词干构成，transfuse 与 transfusional 建在同一基础上。

latinIntro.en: Latin transfundere means to pour across, from trans-, across, and fundere, to pour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 transfundere 意为倒过去，由 trans-（越过）与 fundere（倒）构成。

items.example: The prefix trans- carries the across meaning.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 带「越过」之义。

items.example: Fundere supplies the pouring image.
items.exampleCN: fundere 提供「倒」的意象。

items.meaning: the stem of fundere seen in its supine fusum
items.meaningCN: fundere 的词干，见于其目的分词 fusum
items.example: The stem fus- appears in transfusion.
items.exampleCN: 词干 fus- 出现在 transfusion 中。

items.meaning: to pour from one vessel into another
items.meaningCN: 把液体从一器皿倒进另一器皿
items.example: Transfundere joins across to pour.
items.exampleCN: transfundere 把「越过」与「倒」结合起来。

items.example: Transfusio is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: transfusio 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: to transfer blood or fluid into a vein
items.example: Surgeons transfuse blood during heavy bleeding.
items.exampleCN: 大量出血时外科医生会给病人输血。

items.meaning: the act or amount of pouring across
items.example: Transfusion names the act and the unit given.
items.exampleCN: transfusion 兼指动作与输入的量。

items.example: Transfusional medicine studies reactions.
items.exampleCN: 输血医学研究输血反应。

items.meaning: the return of blood collected from the same patient
items.example: Autotransfusion avoids the need for a donor.
items.exampleCN: 自体输血可避免寻找供血者。

items.meaning: the slow introduction of fluid into a vein
items.example: Infusion shares the fundere stem but takes in- instead of trans-.
items.exampleCN: infusion 共享 fundere 词干，但用 in- 而非 trans-。

definition_en: a stitch or thread used to close a wound, the act of closing a wound in this way, or the seam where bones meet
core_image: 一根细线穿过裂口两侧，把皮肉拉拢在一起
scene: 医生清理完伤口，用一根细线把它缝合起来。After cleaning the wound, the doctor used a suture to close it.
sceneCN: 这里 suture 是「缝线」（第 1 个义项：缝合伤口用的线）；句意：医生清理完伤口，用一根细线把它缝合起来。

derivatives.zh: suture 加 -al，义为「缝的；骨缝的」，多用于解剖学
suture 加 -ing，义为「缝合」，指用线闭合组织的操作
suture 加 -less（没有），义为「免缝合的」，指不用缝线闭合伤口

senses.title: The thread that closes a wound
senses.definition: a thread or stitch used by a surgeon to hold the edges of a wound together
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生用来把伤口两侧拉在一起的线或一针
senses.example: The nurse counted every suture before the wound was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口闭合前，护士清点了每一根缝线。
senses.why: Latin sutura means a sewing, so the word first names the thread that does the sewing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sutura 意为「缝」，所以这个词先指用来缝的那根线。

senses.title: The act of stitching tissue
senses.definition: the act of joining the edges of a wound or incision with stitches
senses.definitionCN: 用缝线把伤口或切口的边缘连起来的动作
senses.example: The resident practised suturing on a pad of false skin.
senses.exampleCN: 住院医师在假皮垫上练习缝合。
senses.why: The same noun also names the action, because a sewing is both the thread and the work of sewing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也指动作，因为「缝」既是线，也是缝这件事。

senses.title: The seam between skull bones
senses.definition: a line where two bones of the skull are joined by thin fibrous tissue
senses.definitionCN: 颅骨两块骨头之间由薄纤维组织相连的接缝
senses.example: The skull sutures allow the head to grow in childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 颅骨骨缝让头部在童年时期得以生长。
senses.why: Bones that meet along a wavy line look like two pieces of cloth sewn together, so anatomy borrowed the sewing word.
senses.whyCN: 沿波浪线相接的骨头看起来像两块布缝在一起，解剖学便借用了这个「缝」的词。

senses.title: A planned method of closure
senses.definition: a chosen surgical method of closing tissue, such as immediate or delayed closure
senses.definitionCN: 选定的缝合方式，如立即缝合或延迟缝合
senses.example: The team chose a delayed suture for the infected wound.
senses.exampleCN: 对于感染的伤口，团队选择了延迟缝合。
senses.why: Once stitching becomes a planned step, the word also names the technique and its timing.
senses.whyCN: 当缝合成为计划好的一步，这个词也指这种技术及其时机。

intro.en: Suture goes straight back to Latin sutura, a sewing or a seam, from suere, to sew.
intro.cn: suture 直接来自拉丁语 sutura（缝、接缝），源自动词 suere（缝）。

items.en: Suere means to sew or stitch, with the supine sutum supplying the stem.
items.cn: suere 意为缝、缀，其目的分词 sutum 提供词干。

items.en: Sutura is a sewing or a seam, built with the noun suffix -ura.
items.cn: sutura 由名词后缀 -ura 构成，意为缝或接缝。

items.en: Medical Latin uses sutura for the joining of tissue and for the seams between skull bones.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 sutura 指组织的连接，也指颅骨之间的骨缝。

items.en: English takes suture first for the seam between bones of the skull.
items.cn: 英语最初用 suture 指颅骨之间的骨缝。

items.en: The word widens to the act of sewing and later to the thread used by surgeons.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到缝合的动作，后来又指外科医生用的线。

items.en: Absorbable threads make suturing a routine step in almost every operation.
items.cn: 可吸收线使缝合成为几乎每台手术的常规步骤。

note.en: Suture is the Latin sewing word, close to its own family and to ordinary stitch words.
note.cn: suture 是拉丁语中表示「缝」的词，与自己的词族以及日常的「缝」义词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a suture or to a bony seam
the act of closing tissue with stitches
closed with a stitch or stitches
a single short piece of thread used to close a wound
the line where two pieces are joined together
the act of closing a wound or opening

normalIntro.en: Suture carries the Latin verb for sewing, and its meanings follow the thread, the act, and the seam.
normalIntro.cn: suture 带着拉丁语「缝」的动词，含义顺着线、动作、接缝三边走。

normal.en: Latin suere means to sew, and sutura means a seam, so the word is a sewing throughout.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 suere 意为缝，sutura 意为接缝，这个词始终是「缝」。

normal.en: The noun is both the thread and the act; the verb is to close a wound.
normal.cn: 名词既指线也指动作，动词则是缝合伤口。

normal.en: Absorbable sutures dissolve, so nobody has to remove them.
normal.cn: 可吸收缝线会自行溶解，所以不必拆线。

normal.en: A suture line is the row of stitches left on the skin.
normal.cn: suture line 是皮肤上留下的一排缝线。

normal.en: Skull sutures borrow the sewing image for the seams between bone plates.
normal.cn: 颅骨骨缝借「缝」的意象来指骨板之间的接缝。

abstract.en: Picture a fine thread drawn through two edges of skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线穿过皮肤的两侧边缘。

abstract.en: Picture a curved needle arcing through tissue, then a knot pulled tight.
abstract.cn: 想象弯针划过组织，随后一个结被拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture two skull plates meeting along a wavy line.
abstract.cn: 想象两块颅骨板沿一条波浪线相接。

examples.en: The surgeon placed a suture in the small cut on her hand.
examples.cn: 外科医生在她手上的小伤口缝了一针。

examples.en: Absorbable sutures dissolve on their own after a few weeks.
examples.cn: 可吸收缝线在几周后会自行溶解。

examples.en: The skull sutures show as thin wavy lines on the scan.
examples.cn: 颅骨骨缝在影像上显示为细细的波浪线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏彻」——伤口要缝得彻底；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 suere（缝）→ sutura（缝、接缝）→ 英语 suture，核心义「用线把两片缝在一起」，既指动作，也指所用的线与留下的接缝。

sensesIntro.en: Suture moves from the thread, to the act of sewing, to the bony seam that looks sewn, and finally to the planned technique of closure.
sensesIntro.cn: suture 从「线」走到「缝的动作」，再走到看起来像缝出来的骨缝，最后指计划好的缝合术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread pulling two edges of tissue together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线把两侧组织拉拢。

branches.en: The thread itself is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 线本身是最具体的义项。

branches.en: The work of sewing is the action sense.
branches.cn: 缝的动作是行为义项。

branches.en: A bony seam is the image applied to anatomy.
branches.cn: 骨缝是把这一意象用到解剖学。

branches.en: A planned closure is the technique sense.
branches.cn: 计划好的闭合是技术义项。

branches.en: A stitch and a closure plan both describe how tissue is joined.
branches.cn: 一针与一套闭合方案都在讲组织如何被连起来。

intro.en: Suture is Latin sutura, a sewing, from suere, to sew; English adds sutural, suturing, and sutureless.
intro.cn: suture 是拉丁语 sutura（缝），源自 suere（缝）；英语又构成 sutural、suturing 与 sutureless。

latinIntro.en: Latin suere means to sew, and its noun sutura means a seam or the act of sewing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 suere 意为缝，其名词 sutura 意为接缝或缝的动作。

items.example: Suere gives the whole family its sewing image.
items.exampleCN: suere 为整个词族提供「缝」的意象。

items.meaning: the stem of suere seen in its supine sutum
items.meaningCN: suere 的词干，见于其目的分词 sutum
items.example: The stem sut- carries the sewing sense.
items.exampleCN: 词干 sut- 承载「缝」的含义。

items.meaning: forms nouns of result or action
items.meaningCN: 构成表示结果或动作的名词
items.example: The suffix -ura turns suere into sutura.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ura 把 suere 变成 sutura。

items.example: Sutura is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: sutura 是英语词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a stitch, the thread, or a bony seam
items.example: Suture names the thread and the seam.
items.exampleCN: suture 兼指缝线与接缝。

items.meaning: to close a wound with stitches
items.example: Surgeons suture deep cuts in layers.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生分层缝合深伤口。

items.example: Sutural lines mark the skull plates.
items.exampleCN: 骨缝线标出颅骨各板的位置。

items.meaning: the act of closing tissue with stitches
items.example: Suturing takes steady hands and good light.
items.exampleCN: 缝合需要稳定的手和良好的照明。

items.example: A sutureless clip closed the small cut.
items.exampleCN: 一枚免缝合夹闭合了小伤口。

definition_en: a small sharp knife with a thin blade, used by surgeons and anatomists for cutting tissue
core_image: 一把窄薄的小刀，刀锋在灯下反出一道亮线
scene: 主刀医生伸出手，接过护士递来的手术刀。The surgeon held out a hand and took the scalpel from the nurse.
sceneCN: 这里 scalpel 是「手术刀」（第 1 个义项：外科切开组织用的刀）；句意：主刀医生伸出手，接过护士递来的手术刀。

derivatives.zh: 与 scalpel 同出拉丁语 scalpere（刻），义为「雕刻；塑形」
sculpt 加 -ure，义为「雕刻；雕塑品」，与 scalpel 共享「刻」的词根
scalpel 加 -like（像……的），义为「手术刀般的；极锋利的」

senses.title: The knife a surgeon cuts with
senses.definition: a short knife with a very sharp, thin blade used to make surgical incisions
senses.definitionCN: 刀刃极薄极利、用来做外科切口的短刀
senses.example: The scrub nurse slapped the scalpel into the surgeon palm.
senses.exampleCN: 器械护士把手术刀拍进外科医生掌心。
senses.why: Latin scalpellum is a little knife, and the operating theatre keeps that literal sense of a small blade for cutting flesh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 scalpellum 意为小刀，手术室里保留了这个字面义：切开皮肉的小刀。

senses.title: The knife of the anatomy room
senses.definition: a fine blade used to separate and display parts of a dead body or a specimen
senses.definitionCN: 用来分离并展示遗体或标本各部分的精细刀
senses.example: Students learn to hold a scalpel before they touch a specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在接触标本之前先学会握解剖刀。
senses.why: Because the blade cuts cleanly at a small scale, anatomy adopted it for careful separation rather than for speed.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种刀能在很小的尺度上切得干净，解剖学便用它来细致分离，而不是求快。

senses.title: A sharp tool of criticism
senses.titleCN: 犀利的剖析；锋利的批判
senses.definition: something used to cut an argument or a text apart with great precision
senses.definitionCN: 用来把论点或文本精确剖开的比喻性工具
senses.example: Her review used a scalpel on every weak claim in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她的评论像手术刀一样剖开论文里每一处薄弱的论断。
senses.why: A blade that separates tissue neatly becomes a figure for analysis that separates truth from error without tearing it.
senses.whyCN: 能整齐分开组织的刀，成了「把真与误干净分开而不撕碎」的分析比喻。

intro.en: Scalpel comes from Latin scalpellum, a little knife, the diminutive of scalprum, a cutting tool, from scalpere, to cut or carve.
intro.cn: scalpel 来自拉丁语 scalpellum（小刀），是 scalprum（刀具）的指小形式，而 scalprum 源自动词 scalpere（切、刻）。

items.en: Scalpere means to cut or carve, and it also lies behind words for carving.
items.cn: scalpere 意为切、刻，也是表示雕刻的一批词的来源。

items.en: Scalprum names a cutting tool, a knife or a chisel.
items.cn: scalprum 指切削工具，即刀或凿。

items.en: Scalpellum is the diminutive of scalprum, so it means a little knife.
items.cn: scalpellum 是 scalprum 的指小形式，意为小刀。

items.en: Roman medical writers use scalpellum for the small blade of surgery.
items.cn: 罗马医学作家用 scalpellum 指外科用的小刀。

items.en: English adopts scalpel for the surgeon small knife.
items.cn: 英语借入 scalpel，指外科医生用的小刀。

items.en: Blade and handle become separate standard parts, and disposable blades keep a sterile edge.
items.cn: 刀片与刀柄分成标准部件，一次性刀片则保持无菌的锋口。

note.en: Scalpel looks like scalp but shares its root with sculpt and sculpture, and it sits beside other cutting instruments.
note.cn: scalpel 与 scalp 只是拼写相像，真正的同根词是 sculpt 与 sculpture；它也与其它切割器械相邻。

entries.definition: the skin covering the top of the head
entries.definitionCN: 头皮；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to carve or shape a material into a form
a carved or shaped work of art
a blade with a handle used for cutting
a small pointed surgical blade used for a tiny cut
the flat cutting part of a tool

normalIntro.en: Scalpel is a little carving knife: Latin scalpere cuts, scalprum is the tool, and scalpellum shrinks it.
normalIntro.cn: scalpel 是一把小小的刻刀：拉丁语 scalpere 是切，scalprum 是刀具，scalpellum 把它缩小。

normal.en: Latin scalpere means to carve, so a scalpel is a knife for carving living tissue.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 scalpere 意为刻，所以 scalpel 就是用来「刻」活体组织的刀。

normal.en: The ending -ellum is a diminutive, so scalpellum is a small scalprum.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ellum 表指小，因此 scalpellum 就是小一号的 scalprum。

normal.en: A scalpel blade is the cutting part, and the handle is gripped in the palm.
normal.cn: scalpel blade 是切割的部分，刀柄握在掌中。

normal.en: Scalpel and sculpture share the carving root: one cuts flesh, the other cuts stone.
normal.cn: scalpel 与 sculpture 共享「刻」的词根：一个切肉，一个刻石。

normal.en: A disposable scalpel comes sterile and is thrown away after one use.
normal.cn: 一次性手术刀出厂无菌，用一次就丢弃。

abstract.en: Picture a thin steel blade catching a line of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一片薄薄的钢刃映出一道亮线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a small knife above a pale specimen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握着小小的刀，悬在苍白的标本上方。

abstract.en: Picture a critic slicing a weak argument into neat strips.
abstract.cn: 想象评论者把薄弱的论证切成整齐的细条。

examples.en: The nurse passed the scalpel to the surgeon without a word.
examples.cn: 护士一言不发地把手术刀递给外科医生。

examples.en: A scalpel blade is swapped out as soon as it feels dull.
examples.cn: 手术刀片一变钝就会被换掉。

examples.en: The anatomist used a scalpel to expose the nerve.
examples.cn: 解剖学家用解剖刀暴露出那条神经。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯开剖」——轻轻一划就剖开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scalpere（切、刻）→ scalprum（刀具、凿子）→ 指小形式 scalpellum（小刀）→ 英语 scalpel，核心义「用来切开的窄薄小刀」。

sensesIntro.en: Scalpel moves from the operating knife, to the fine blade of the anatomy room, and then to a figure for precise criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: scalpel 从手术室里的刀，走到解剖室里的精细刀，再成为「精确剖析」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow blade that opens tissue along a clean line.
core.cn: 核心意象：窄薄的刀刃沿线干净地打开组织。

branches.en: The surgical knife is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 手术刀是字面义项。

branches.en: The anatomy blade is the same knife used to separate parts.
branches.cn: 解剖刀是同一把刀用于分离各部位。

branches.en: Precise criticism is the figurative branch.
branches.cn: 精确的批判是比喻分支。

branches.en: Surgeon and anatomist both need a clean, small edge.
branches.cn: 外科医生与解剖学家都需要干净而小的锋口。

branches.en: Cutting flesh and cutting an argument share the same neat separation.
branches.cn: 切开皮肉与剖开论证共享「整齐分开」这一动作。

intro.en: Scalpel is the Latin diminutive scalpellum, while sculpt and sculpture share the carving root behind it.
intro.cn: scalpel 是拉丁语指小形式 scalpellum，而 sculpt 与 sculpture 共享它背后的「刻」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin scalpere means to cut or carve; scalprum is a cutting tool and scalpellum is its diminutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scalpere 意为切、刻；scalprum 是刀具，scalpellum 是它的指小形式。

items.example: Scalpere supplies the cutting image of the family.
items.exampleCN: scalpere 提供这个词族的「切」意象。

items.meaning: a cutting tool, a knife or chisel
items.example: Scalprum names the tool itself.
items.exampleCN: scalprum 指工具本身。

items.meaning: a little knife, the diminutive of scalprum
items.example: Scalpellum is the direct source of scalpel.
items.exampleCN: scalpellum 是 scalpel 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ellum makes the knife small.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ellum 把刀变小。

items.example: Scalpel keeps the small-knife sense.
items.exampleCN: scalpel 保留「小刀」的含义。

items.meaning: as sharp or as precise as a scalpel
items.example: A scalpel-like focus cuts to the point.
items.exampleCN: 手术刀般的专注能直切要点。

items.meaning: to carve or shape a material
items.example: Sculpt shares the Latin carving root.
items.exampleCN: sculpt 共享拉丁语「刻」的词根。

items.example: Sculpture cuts stone; a scalpel cuts tissue.
items.exampleCN: sculpture 刻石头，手术刀切组织。

items.example: The sculptor works with a chisel, not a blade.
items.exampleCN: 雕刻家用凿子，而不是手术刀。

definition_en: tending to grow and spread without control, or showing deep harmful intent
core_image: 一团暗影从墙角迅速蔓延，吞没周围的光
scene: 医生看着影像片，神情严肃地讨论肿瘤的性质。The doctor studied the scan and spoke gravely about a malignant tumour.
sceneCN: 这里 malignant 是「恶性的」（第 1 个义项：肿瘤或细胞不受控制地生长并可能转移）；句意：医生看着影像片，严肃地谈到一个恶性肿瘤。

derivatives.zh: malignant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「恶性；恶性肿瘤」
否定前缀 non- 加 malignant 构成，义为「非恶性的」
前缀 pre-（之前）加 malignant 构成，义为「癌前的；恶性病变前的」

senses.title: Cancerous and spreading
senses.definition: describing a tumour or cell that grows without control and can spread to other parts of the body
senses.definitionCN: 描述不受控制地生长、并能转移到身体其他部位的肿瘤或细胞
senses.example: Surgeons removed the malignant growth from her liver.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生切除了她肝脏上的恶性肿瘤。
senses.why: Latin malignus means evil-natured, and medicine borrowed that sense for tissue that behaves like an invading enemy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 malignus 意为天性恶的，医学借这个意思指像入侵敌人一样行为的组织。

senses.title: Severe and life-threatening
senses.definition: describing a disease that is severe, progressive, and likely to cause death
senses.definitionCN: 描述严重、持续进展并可能致命的疾病
senses.example: Malignant hypertension can damage the kidneys within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性高血压可能在几周内损害肾脏。
senses.why: A disease that refuses to stop and destroys the body looks evil in the old moral metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 不肯停止、不断摧毁身体的疾病，在古老的道德比喻中显得像「恶」一样。

senses.title: Deeply harmful
senses.definition: having a destructive influence on people, institutions, or events
senses.definitionCN: 对人、制度或事件产生破坏性影响
senses.example: The report exposed a malignant culture inside the agency.
senses.exampleCN: 报告揭露了该机构内部一种有害的文化。
senses.why: The moral sense of evil broadens from a person to any force that corrupts what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 「恶」的道德含义从人扩展到任何侵蚀其接触对象的力量。

senses.title: Full of ill will
senses.definition: showing intense spite or a desire to hurt someone
senses.definitionCN: 表现出强烈的怨恨或伤害他人的欲望
senses.example: He answered with a malignant smile that chilled the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着恶意的微笑回答，让全场发冷。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a person of evil nature, and a look or smile is the visible sign of that nature.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指天性恶的人，而目光或微笑是这种天性的外在迹象。

senses.title: Threatening and ominous
senses.definition: threatening great harm in a way that feels like evil at work
senses.definitionCN: 以仿佛邪恶在作祟的方式预示巨大伤害
senses.example: A malignant silence filled the abandoned ward.
senses.exampleCN: 废弃病房里弥漫着不祥的寂静。
senses.why: Writers extend the evil-nature sense to atmospheres and places that seem to promise harm.
senses.whyCN: 作家把「天性恶」扩展到似乎预示伤害的氛围与场所。

intro.en: Malignant comes from Latin malignus, evil-natured, generally explained as male, badly, plus the root of gignere, to beget; Old French malignant brought it into English.
intro.cn: malignant 来自拉丁语 malignus（天性恶的），一般认为由 male（坏地）与 gignere（生出）的词根构成；古法语 malignant 把它带入英语。

items.en: Male is an adverb meaning badly or ill.
items.cn: male 是意为「坏地、不善地」的副词。

items.en: Gignere means to beget or bring forth, and is generally linked to the second element of malignus.
items.cn: gignere 意为生育、产生，一般认为与 malignus 的第二部分有关。

items.en: Malignus describes a person or thing of evil nature.
items.cn: malignus 描述天性恶的人或事物。

items.en: Malignant is the present participle of malignier, to act with evil intent.
items.cn: malignant 是动词 malignier（存心作恶）的现在分词。

items.en: English adopts malignant first for evil intent and later for dangerous disease.
items.cn: 英语先用 malignant 表示恶意，后来才用于危险的疾病。

items.en: Pathology makes the medical sense of invasive growth the dominant one.
items.cn: 病理学使「侵袭性生长」这一医学义项成为主要用法。

note.en: Malignant shares its Latin stem with malign and malignancy, and stands opposite benign in medicine while sitting near malicious in the language of ill will.
note.cn: malignant 与 malign、malignancy 共享拉丁词干，在医学上与 benign 相对，在表达恶意时又与 malicious 相邻。

entries.definition: to speak evil of, or evil in nature
the state of being malignant, or a malignant tumour
in a malignant manner
not cancerous, or gentle in nature
relating to or caused by cancer
intending to harm someone

normalIntro.en: Malignant joins bad to birth: a nature that was born bad and keeps growing worse.
normalIntro.cn: malignant 把「坏」与「生」连在一起：一种天生就坏、还不断恶化的天性。

normal.en: A malignant tumour is not benign and can spread.
normal.cn: 恶性肿瘤不是良性的，而且可能转移。

normal.en: Malignant cells divide without normal limits.
normal.cn: 恶性细胞不受正常限制地分裂。

normal.en: The noun malignancy names the condition or the growth.
normal.cn: 名词 malignancy 指这种病变或肿瘤本身。

normal.en: Benign is the opposite of malignant in medical reports.
normal.cn: 在医学报告中，benign 是 malignant 的反义词。

normal.en: Malicious describes the will to hurt; malignant adds a deep, growing evil.
normal.cn: malicious 指伤人的意图，malignant 则多一层深重且不断滋长的恶。

abstract.en: Picture a dark stain spreading across a white wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一块暗色污迹在白墙上不断扩散。

abstract.en: Imagine a fire that no water can stop once it starts.
abstract.cn: 想象一场一旦燃起就浇不灭的火。

abstract.en: Think of a quiet poison leaking into a clear well.
abstract.cn: 想象一种无声的毒物渗入清澈的水井。

examples.en: The biopsy confirmed that the lump was malignant.
examples.cn: 活检确认这个肿块是恶性的。

examples.en: Malignant cells can travel through the blood to other organs.
examples.cn: 恶性细胞可以通过血液转移到其他器官。

examples.en: He gave the proposal a malignant review that attacked every point.
examples.cn: 他对这份提案作了恶意的评论，逐条攻击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫良」——没有良心，就会生出恶意；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 male（坏地）+ gignere（生出）→ malignus（天性恶的）→ 古法语 malignant → 英语 malignant，核心义「天生带恶、不断扩散」。

sensesIntro.en: Malignant starts from a tumour that grows like an enemy, passes to severe disease, then to any harmful force, to visible ill will, and finally to an ominous atmosphere.
sensesIntro.cn: malignant 从像敌人一样生长的肿瘤出发，转到严重的疾病，再到任何有害的力量、可见的恶意，最后到不祥的氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark patch spreading from a corner and swallowing the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团暗影从墙角迅速蔓延，吞没周围的光。

branches.en: The cancerous growth is the dominant medical branch.
branches.cn: 癌性增生是占主导的医学分支。

branches.en: Severe disease is the clinical severity branch.
branches.cn: 严重疾病是临床严重程度的分支。

branches.en: Harmful influence is the moral force branch.
branches.cn: 有害影响是道德力量的分支。

branches.en: Visible ill will is the personal branch.
branches.cn: 可见的恶意是个人层面的分支。

branches.en: The ominous atmosphere is the literary branch.
branches.cn: 不祥氛围是文学分支。

intro.en: Malignant joins the Latin root for bad to a root for begetting, and the same material yields malign, malignancy, and malignantly.
intro.cn: malignant 把拉丁语表示「坏」的词根与表示「生」的词根结合，同一套材料还产出 malign、malignancy 与 malignantly。

latinIntro.en: Latin male means badly, gignere means to beget, and malignus means evil-natured; benignus, kind-natured, is its mirror image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 male 意为坏地，gignere 意为生出，malignus 意为天性恶的；表示天性善的 benignus 是它的镜像。

items.example: Male supplies the bad half of malignus.
items.exampleCN: male 提供 malignus 中表示「坏」的那一半。

items.example: Gignere is generally linked to the second half of malignus.
items.exampleCN: gignere 一般认为与 malignus 的后半部分有关。

items.example: Malignus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: malignus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Benignus is built with bene, well, as the mirror of malignus.
items.exampleCN: benignus 用 bene（好地）构成，是 malignus 的镜像。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ant turns the participle into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 把这个分词变成英语形容词。

items.example: Malignant describes both tumours and intentions.
items.exampleCN: malignant 既描述肿瘤，也描述意图。

items.example: Malign is the shorter relative of malignant.
items.exampleCN: malign 是 malignant 更短的亲缘词。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms malignancy from malignant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 从 malignant 构成 malignancy。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns malignant into malignantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 malignant 变成 malignantly。

items.example: Premalignant changes can be detected early.
items.exampleCN: 癌前病变可以早期发现。

items.example: Nonmalignant growths are usually harmless.
items.exampleCN: 非恶性增生通常无害。
